spots.bio: Tree-draped beach south of Taveuni's airstrip, good for both snorkelling and swimming.
spots.notes: Frommer's (spelled Beverly) lists it with Prince Charles and Valaca beaches as snorkelling and swimming spots south of the airstrip. No Wikipedia article; Rough Guides not read. Free/open is inferred for a public beach.
unverified: no fee or access arrangement sourced (customary landowner access possible)
'near Matei' cut: Frommers says south of the airstrip; free/open inferred

spots.ticket_reason: no official operator site found (village-run, booked in advance)
spots.bio: Guided 7 km full-day hike through Taveuni's rainforest to archaeological sites and viewpoints, ending at Tavoro waterfall.
spots.notes: Wikivoyage: $40 with guide, booking in advance necessary, full day 7 km. Currency assumed FJD (Fiji dollars) as Wikivoyage writes $.

spots.bio: Natural rock slide on a Taveuni stream where visitors swim in cool water and slide down the smooth rock.
spots.notes: Wikivoyage advises waiting for locals to show where to start and check there is enough water. No fee mentioned.
unverified: no fee sourced; a local or landowner charge is possible
Frommers: admission free (Waitavaia Sliding Rocks near Waiyevo)

spots.bio: Colonial Romanesque Catholic church on a hill at Wairiki, overlooking the beach of a famed canoe battle against Tongan invaders.
spots.notes: Wikivoyage calls it the most architecturally interesting building on Taveuni, also known as the Taveuni Catholic Church.

spots.bio: Town on Vanua Levu's south coast with a yacht club at the old Copra Shed, diving and geothermal hot springs.
spots.notes: Wikipedia: hot springs (Nakama, made a tourist attraction in 2022), Copra Shed Marina and yacht club, diving and yachting. Wikivoyage: popular for diving and yachting. Pin: use town centre place=town, not Wikivoyage district point.

spots.bio: Rainforest reserve northwest of Savusavu, co-managed by its community, with walking trails, rare birds and endemic frogs.
spots.notes: National Trust of Fiji page (title 'Waisali Rainforest | National Trust of Fiji'): adult FJ$3.00, child 12 and under $1.00, 5 and under free; 30 min drive NW of Savusavu; birds and frogs. Size: 120 ha per BirdLife and the Trust, 130 ha in one travel site; omitted from bio. Waterfall not confirmed on the Trust page; bio mention comes from the draft only. Not covered by any park pass.
unverified: waterfall not confirmed from fetched page
